knowledgePoint.title: Finding the Cross Product Equation of a Line That Passes Through Two Points

response.markdown: A line passes through the points  $P(-3,-1,4)$ and $Q(1,8,9).$ Find its vector equation in the form $r\times v=c.$
response.solution:
Local correction by Codex. The five original Math Academy choices are retained; the additional correct equation is locally authored. Math Academy's grading key for the original bank is unconfirmed.

We need a vector parallel to the line. Using the two given points,

$$
v=q-p=\begin{bmatrix}1\\8\\9\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}-3\\-1\\4\end{bmatrix}
=\begin{bmatrix}4\\9\\5\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Starting with $(r-p)\times v=0$, we obtain $r\times v=p\times v$. Expanding the cross product gives

$$
p\times v=\begin{vmatrix}i&j&k\\-3&-1&4\\4&9&5\end{vmatrix}
=(-5-36)i-( -15-16)j+(-27+4)k=-41i+31j-23k.
$$

Thus the equation is

$$
r\times\begin{bmatrix}4\\9\\5\end{bmatrix}=-41i+31j-23k.
$$

Both given points satisfy this equation: $P\times v=Q\times v=(-41,31,-23)$. None of the five original choices does.

Original Math Academy explanation (preserved verbatim below; its concluding signs are incorrect):

We know that the line passes through the points $P(-3,-1,4)$ and $Q(1,8,9).$ Now, we need to find a vector parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =q-p \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 8 \\ 9\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 9 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, starting with the equation of the line using the cross product, we manipulate the equation and then substitute in our values of $p$ and $v$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\times v & =0 \\ r\times v-p\times v & =0 \\ r\times v & =p\times v \\ r\times \begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 9 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}\times \begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 9 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} \\ r\times \begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 9 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ -3 & -1 & 4 \\ 4 & 9 & 5\end{vmatrix} \\ r\times \begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 9 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} & =-41i-31j+23k.\end{aligned}
$$
